title: Sub-Scope Report Customisation Architecture
summary: define the docs_subscope default, registered collection customisations, toolbar ownership, public isolation, and lifecycle integration
content_html:
Sub-Scope Report Customisation Architecture

Architecture Outcome

Every configured one-level sub-scope uses the same docs_subscope engine and one useful default. A sub-scope may select a registered customisation module when its own content or workflow needs more than that default.

configured collection
  -> docs_subscope engine
  -> default presentation and Manage actions
  -> optional registered collection customisation

The customisation is an explicit property of the collection, not an inferred variant of viewer_report, a filename convention, or a condition on a known scope or sub-scope ID.

Collection And Host Identity

The collection remains {scope, sub_scope}. Child documents remain exact {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} targets.

The indexed host is an ordinary parent-scope document containing:

viewer_report: docs_subscope
viewer_report_access: local
viewer_report_subscope: <sub-scope-id>

The host selects the engine and collection only. The configured sub-scope record selects a known customisation identity; absence means the default. Config must never contain an arbitrary JavaScript module path.

Definition Of The Default

The default is the complete minimum useful report for an ordinary flat document collection. It is not Analysis/Tags with optional labels removed.

Shared public-safe behaviour:

  • collection validation and ordered membership;
  • list, detail, empty, unavailable, and error states;
  • title search over the loaded collection;
  • validated by-ID loading and subdoc navigation; and
  • clean absence of management controls.

Default Manage behaviour adds:

  • status and non-viewable presentation from the compact Manage row;
  • title-ascending initial order and a two-state sort control switching between title ascending and last_updated descending;
  • exact-collection New document, including for an empty collection;
  • collection-local checkbox selection, Select all, Clear, and Done;
  • the Actions menu and checked-ID Prepare Package;
  • validated-detail Delete and Copy Link;
  • mounted collection/detail publication for the app-level Import owner; and
  • capability-aware omitted or disabled states without target fallback.

The recency order places missing or unusable last_updated values after dated records, then uses title ascending and doc_id as deterministic tie-breakers. Changing sort does not change checked IDs. Select all and Shift-range consume the current visible sorted projection.

Copy Link follows the existing main-index convention: it copies a Markdown link whose label is the document title and whose destination is the exact viewer URL for the validated sub-scope document, including its report host and subdoc identity. It does not copy a source, payload, or management-service URL.

Filters beyond title search, additional columns, additional row fields, and additional actions are customisations. A customisation may add to the default; it does not silently remove or replace default behaviour.

The public manifest remains:

{
  "docs": [
    {"doc_id": "d-*", "title": "Title"}
  ]
}

The standard Manage row is:

{
  "doc_id": "d-*",
  "title": "Title",
  "ui_status": "",
  "viewable": true,
  "last_updated": "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"
}

last_updated is standard because the default visibly consumes it for recency sorting. The Manage manifest remains a data projection, not an action registry.

Isolated Candidate And Cutover

SSR-1 develops the default through an explicitly temporary local-only report identity, provisionally docs_subscope_candidate.

The candidate copies the current shared report module so work on its structure cannot regress the canonical docs_subscope used by Analysis/Tags. Copying the report module alone is insufficient: the Manage host currently gives every docs_subscope the same contribution containing New, selection, Prepare Package, Delete, row state, and Import-context publication. The candidate must therefore receive its own default Manage composition as well.

The isolation boundary is narrow:

  • copy the shared report module that is being reworked;
  • add a local-only loader and explicit temporary Manage dispatch;
  • create a new default Manage contribution rather than changing the existing Tags-shaped contribution in place;
  • reuse generic filter, URL, target, action, selection, and lifecycle helpers where their contracts already fit; and
  • reuse the one sub-scope builder and its public/Manage manifest generation.

The candidate is not added to the public report loader. Its Studio host uses the temporary report ID only while SSR-1 is active; final host front matter uses canonical viewer_report: docs_subscope.

Cutover occurs only after the studio/default empty/list/detail/action surface is accepted and Analysis/Tags passes parity through its registered customisation. In the same delivery:

  1. canonical docs_subscope resolves the accepted implementation;
  2. the Studio fixture host switches to canonical docs_subscope;
  3. Analysis/Tags switches to canonical default plus its customisation; and
  4. the candidate report registry row, loader entry, temporary Manage dispatch, and superseded module/contribution wiring are removed.

There is no permanent alias and no runtime condition on sub_scope: default.

Persistence And Propagation

The default is persisted as one canonical implementation, not as a copied report attached to each sub-scope. studio/default remains a permanent local reference instance, but it is not the source of the implementation.

concern canonical authority
Shared list/detail behaviour Canonical docs_subscope runtime module
Default Manage controls and lifecycle publication Canonical default Manage contribution
Default public and Manage manifest fields Shared sub-scope builder
One collection instance Sub-scope config, report-host document, and child source documents
Additional collection behaviour Registered customisation selected by that sub-scope
Default review and regression surface Permanent studio/default reference instance

An ordinary live instance persists only its collection and host identity:

report host: viewer_report = docs_subscope
report host: viewer_report_subscope = projects
sub-scope config: no customisation identity

It does not receive a JavaScript copy or version of the default. Each mount loads the current canonical docs_subscope implementation. Absence of a customisation identity selects the default path, so an uncustomised dotlineform/projects and any later lifecycle-created collection receive the same implementation automatically.

Generated manifest.json and manage-manifest.json files persist one collection's current data projection. They are not templates, code, or the definition of the default and must not be hand-maintained as such.

Changes propagate through their owning layer:

  • a shared list/detail or presentation change updates the canonical report module and reaches every mounted instance when current assets are loaded;
  • a default management change updates the canonical default Manage contribution and reaches every manageable instance;
  • a default manifest-field change updates the shared builder and requires the affected configured sub-scopes to be rebuilt so their generated projections match the runtime contract;
  • a customisation change updates its registered builder/browser parts and affects only collections selecting that identity; and
  • a configuration-shape change also regenerates browser configuration before affected reports are reviewed.

Runtime and builder changes to one manifest contract ship as one coordinated change. The runtime may define contained missing-value behaviour, such as undated rows sorting last, but stale manifests are not a second supported implementation.

Default changes are first exercised on studio/default, then checked against Analysis/Tags as a customised consumer. Changes that alter the public-safe path also receive public-route evidence. After cutover the Studio host uses canonical docs_subscope permanently; only the development candidate and its temporary registry/dispatch are removed.

Customisation Resolution

A controlled registry maps each known customisation identity to its allowed contributions:

sub-scope config identity
  -> safe registry entry
  -> shared/public contribution, when one exists
  -> Manage contribution, when capability and access allow it

Unknown identities fail as configuration errors. Public routes cannot import Manage modules, local capability data, or mutation workflows.

A collection customisation may compose reusable feature helpers, but it owns the decision to include them. The standard contribution contract must cover:

  • row or row-metadata presentation;
  • controls adjacent to default title search;
  • list-toolbar controls;
  • collection-local selection controls and actions;
  • validated-detail controls; and
  • mount, state, refresh, and unmount lifecycle events.

One registered customisation identity may need both a builder-side data projection and browser-side presentation/interaction module. Those parts are registered together under the same code-owned identity. Configuration may select the identity and supply validated settings; it cannot name fields, module paths, or executable handlers arbitrarily.

The builder-side part adds only the data required by that customisation to the Manage or public manifest allowed to carry it. The browser module consumes those fields through standard extension positions. This lets a future Projects module introduce different metadata, filters, columns, or actions without teaching the default engine about Projects or copying the report.

Every rendered action declares a stable identity, placement, target kind, capability requirement, empty-state behaviour, handler owner, and refresh effect. Actions consume only their explicit collection, checked IDs, or validated document target.

Toolbar Ownership

The default Manage contribution owns New, sorting, status/viewability row presentation, selection, Prepare Package, validated-detail Delete and Copy Link, plus collection publication for app-level Import.

An optional customisation owns only its additional controls and presentation. It may reuse common helpers, but those helpers do not activate themselves based on manifest shape or a known collection ID.

The single app-level Import action remains outside the report toolbar. A mounted report may publish its exact collection and refresh callbacks through the standard lifecycle seam; it does not create another Import button.

Analysis/Tags Retrofit

Analysis/Tags becomes one registered customisation of the default report.

The default provides the complete baseline defined above. The Analysis/Tags module adds only its configured group field, group order, and group filter. The builder-side customisation projects group into the Manage manifest; the browser-side customisation renders and applies the group controls. The public manifest remains {doc_id, title} and therefore has no group filter.

Manage title Tags and public title Concepts remain resolved collection configuration, not a new report type. No analysis, tags, concept, or known group value belongs in the default engine or customisation dispatcher.

The refactor removes superseded direct wiring after parity is proven. It does not retain a hidden legacy Tags route alongside the registered module.

Lifecycle Integration

The New sub-scope lifecycle creates a collection with no customisation identity. It also creates one associated parent report host and valid empty public-safe and Manage projections, then refreshes configuration and parent discovery before navigating to the exact returned host.

The association between lifecycle-created collection and host is explicit and stable. Later deletion previews and applies against that exact association; it must not infer the host from title, filename, active document, or URL text.

Post-commit refresh or navigation failure returns the committed identities and retries follow-through only. It never creates another collection or host.

Projects Decision Boundary

The dotlineform/projects collection first receives the default through the normal lifecycle. Its real documents and management workflow are then reviewed before any Projects module is designed.

Possible differences—metadata, grouping, status, sorting, filters, or actions—are evidence prompts, not assumed requirements. The decision may be that the default is sufficient. If customisation is justified, Projects uses the same config identity, registry, contribution positions, exact targets, and public/Manage boundary as Analysis/Tags.

Decisions Owned By Delivery

The first delivery freezes:

  • the exact sub-scope config field and registry shape;
  • the paired builder/browser registration contract for a customisation;
  • contribution placement and lifecycle payloads; and
  • the final module ownership and filenames after current-code inspection.

The default surface, standard Manage row including last_updated, initial title order, recency toggle, Copy Link semantics, and Analysis/Tags group-only customisation are accepted inputs to that remaining contract work.

The second delivery freezes the lifecycle association and failure shape. The third decides only the Projects-specific needs that can be justified from the working default.

The feature parent owns delivery order and status.
